name: Krystal Integrated Services Ltd
title: Krystal Integrated Services Ltd - 544149 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue fell about 12% YoY to INR364.94 crore on selective bidding, while PAT rose 11% to INR18.85 crore; FY26 consolidated order book is about INR2,500 crore+.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was INR364.94 crore, down nearly 12% YoY but up 19% QoQ, as management deliberately skipped low-margin bids. EBITDA excluding other income fell 11% YoY to INR23.78 crore, yet margin edged up 3 bps to 6.51% and PAT grew over 11% YoY to INR18.85 crore. For FY26, revenue rose 5.32% to INR1,277.28 crore, EBITDA rose 7.5% to INR83.53 crore (6.54% margin), and PAT was INR64.35 crore (up nearly 3%). Management guided to upwards of 20% consolidated revenue growth in FY27 and announced the 100% acquisition of Citelum India, its first acquisition, for smart lighting and urban infrastructure.

financial_highlights.change: increased during year; management expects meaningful reduction

segments.name: Government business
segments.commentary: Management is being more selective in bidding; 2 new contracts in Q4 FY26 and 17 for the full year. Mix was about 70:30 government to corporate, with a stated aim to rebalance toward corporate.

segments.name: Corporate business
segments.commentary: Management says corporate margin profile has improved since the pandemic. Management cited 177+ new customers and 250+ new sites added in FY26, with INR300 crore of multi-year new business value.

segments.name: Waste management
segments.commentary: Currently managing more than 350 TPD. Qualification allows bids for about 480-500 TPD by fiscal year-end, with a target of 800-1,000 TPD over 18 months. Vasai Virar MSW win was among top 3 qualifying agencies with technology partner MTS.

segments.name: Citelum India (acquisition)
segments.commentary: Board approved 100% acquisition of Citelum India Pvt Ltd from Citelum S.A.S. (EDF Group). Company is in smart lighting, street lighting, and city O&M, with smart city presence in Ahmedabad, Noida and Chennai. Financial terms and closing timeline were not disclosed on the call.

segments.name: Taskmaster (B2C)
segments.commentary: Start-up B2C residential deep-cleaning platform with FY26 revenue of about INR46 lakh. Management expects traction to begin from Q2 FY27 and will not give a 2-3 year revenue guidance yet.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: upwards of 20% consolidated revenue growth.
Margin appreciation expected, led by corporate mix and higher-margin emerging verticals.
Management says the INR180 crore of business skipped on margin grounds and delayed government decisions will shift into FY27.
Waste management qualification target of 800-1,000 TPD over the next 18 months.
Working capital and loans/advances expected to normalise as new contracts reach steady state.
capex_capacity: Waste management capacity: more than 350 TPD currently; qualified for about 480-500 TPD by end of FY27; target of 800-1,000 TPD over 18 months.
Workforce of over 41,676 on-site staff, with a shift toward skilled and semi-skilled manpower to support higher-value pricing.
Pan-India network of 31 branches, serving 570+ customers across 4,000+ locations.
Bioenzyme waste treatment remains in pilot (Mira-Bhayandar, Vasai Virar) with VPRC Chennai; no commercial cost set yet.
Rooftop solar PV project for government hospitals and medical colleges in Maharashtra marks entry into renewables. No capex quantum disclosed.
demand_pricing: Consolidated order book is about INR2,500 crore+ at 31 March 2026 (about INR2,600 crore cited in Q&A over full contract tenure); standalone order book is about INR1,220 crore.
RFP participation rose from 5-6 corporate RFPs in FY24/FY25 to about 30-31 in FY26.

Key wins: MSEDCL substation O&M (33 kV and below), airport FM at Patna and Vijayawada, Tamil Nadu 167 government hospitals FM, 25 AP government hospitals sanitation, Vasai Virar MSW, Maersk, Fortis, Livspace, Indira IVF, Adani hospitals.
Management says it wins corporate deals against CBRE, JLL, SIS and Sodexo by offering direct service delivery rather than outsourced services.
Q4 revenue decline attributed to about INR180 crore of business not bid for on margin grounds, plus tender decisions pending from previous fiscal.

qa_highlights.question: How does Krystal differentiate from global players such as CBRE, JLL, SIS and Sodexo in large corporate mandates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the services are similar but Krystal is the direct service provider, while global players are property managers that outsource services. Many new customers were won against these players.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 3-5 year vision and business mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Rebalancing the government/corporate mix from about 70:30 by adding corporates, with government growth in waste management, O&M and city infrastructure. Management aims to be a diversified player with all verticals revenue-making and profitable within 5 years.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue has Taskmaster contributed and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 revenue was about INR46 lakh. Pilots are ongoing and traction is expected from Q2 FY27, but no 2-3 year revenue guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: What quantifies the Q4 revenue drop of 11.7% YoY, and is it due to exits, slower orders or tender delays?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR180 crore of business was not bid for to protect margins, and some government tender decisions are pending, which pushed business into later periods. Management says the order book covers this and the shortfall will be made up in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for commercialising bioenzyme technology?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the technology is still in pilot with VPRC Chennai in Mira-Bhayandar and Vasai Virar, and no commercial cost or revenue timeline has been set yet.

risks_watch: Government tender decision delays could keep revenue shifting between quarters; the company says INR180 crore was deferred.
Working capital is stretched: receivables and loans/advances rose during FY26 to INR146.45 crore, and normalisation is not yet evidenced.
Q4 revenue fell about 12% YoY, so FY27 growth of upwards of 20% depends on converting the order book and the deferred pipeline.
Citelum acquisition: deal value, funding, closing timeline and integration risk were not disclosed on the call.
Waste management scale-up to 800-1,000 TPD and bioenzyme commercialisation are still early-stage or unproven.
summary.management_tone: Confident on order book, growth and strategy, with a defensive tone when explaining the Q4 revenue decline. Management was vague on Taskmaster and bioenzyme commercial timelines, and gave no numbers for the Citelum deal.
key_quotes: So, our position on consol basis is much better and crosses even INR2,500 crores.

We are targeting to scale this qualification to 800 to 1,000 tons per day over the next 18 months, which would substantially enhance our revenue potential and also give us the scope to better our margin profile.
There is a -- slight delay in the processes to disclose the decision.
This marks our first acquisition, a strategically significant step that provides us with an established platform to participate in India's city infrastructure development projects.

growth.why: Management targets upwards of 20% consolidated revenue growth in FY27, backed by INR2,500 crore+ consolidated order book, about INR180 crore of deferred business shifting into FY27, and waste-management qualification rising to 480-500 TPD by year-end, though no order-level numbers were given for the 20% target and the Citelum acquisition terms were undisclosed.
